chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic,
And whoever was blind with regards to this, he shall (also) be blind in the Hereafter; and more straying from the way
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is the one who delays himself for the Hajj, meaning Hajj of Al-Islam, until the death comes to him'.

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the Hajj of Islam (the first obligatory pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: Who is the person described as blind in the Hereafter according to this interpretation of Surah Al-Isra?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the 'blind' mentioned in Quran 17:72 as specifically referring to one who procrastinates performing Hajj al-Islam until death arrives, highlighting the danger of delaying obligatory duties. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the urgency of fulfilling pillars of worship when capable, linking spiritual blindness in the Hereafter directly to the neglect of this specific act of devotion.
